answer: One concrete defense is the synchronized liveness burst. Each epoch a rotating committee fires a tide of randomized micro-challenges at every identity at the same instant, and each must return a freshly signed response inside a narrow window while the timing of that signal is logged. A single box hosting many clones cannot answer every burst at once: its latency spikes into one correlated plume and throughput collapses, so the cluster is flagged and bonds slashed. Holding N fakes then needs N separate machines online at once each epoch, a linear N-times hardware cost paid continuously.
